assembled_text: Locked-off static camera for the whole six seconds: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no shake, no cut. Only the people move, at natural steady speed: lines of small figures carry straw baskets of river stones on shoulder poles toward the wooden chamber and walk back empty, a few set stones along the chamber's outer walls, labourers in the timber yard at the left shape beams with wooden mallets, dust drifts slowly across the work area. The organised flow of work is the only action; no single person becomes a focus. Only stones are added, and only against the outside of the chamber walls; the chamber stays open on top; no earth is placed and no mound rises during the shot. Keep everything in the start image unchanged: the same early Silla era, the same clothing and colours, the same faces, the same layout, the same horizon and the same light; nothing new is added to the scene. Wooden tools only. No text, no captions, no subtitles, no watermark, no logo. No modern objects, no metal tools, no utility poles, no buildings appearing. No cloned or repeated faces: every person keeps their own face for the whole shot. Nobody looks at the camera, nobody poses, nobody speaks. No invented ritual steps: no coffin lowering, no offerings placed, no bowing, no procession. The build order never changes: coffin, then wooden chamber, then stones, then earth; nothing is built out of order.
